text:
Rishi Malhotra: hey #help — need a quick sanity check. Finance is asking for a cost-by-route report for last week (Mon–Sun) and ideally model breakdown. What’s the “right” way to export from Console now? also: any gotchas vs invoice totals?

Dev Patel: yep, we’ve got the new export flow in Usage Insights (beta-ish but should be on for internal orgs). Do you have access to Console for the org/project?

Rishi Malhotra: I do (org admin in our internal). I’m in Console but not seeing an obvious “export” on the main Usage page.

Paula Mendes: it’s under **Console → Usage Insights → Routes** (not the generic Usage chart). Once you’re on the route list table there’s an **Export** button top-right.

Rishi Malhotra: found Routes. Export button shows up, nice. When I click it I get options for CSV/JSON + time range. Anything I should pick for Finance?

Logan Wright: CSV is usually easiest for Finance. The export is a bounded report (async job) and includes:
- total cost
- input/output tokens
- cached tokens (if cache hit)
- unit cost fields
- p50/p95 latency + error rate (if you include perf columns)
And you can toggle “include model breakdown” (adds per-model rows per route).

Mei Lin: also note the export is scoped to whatever filters you set in the UI first (time range, project, env, region, deployment mode). So set those before you hit Export.

Rishi Malhotra: cool. Is there a weekly preset? I only see “Last 24h / 7d / 30d / Custom”.

Paula Mendes: use **Custom** and set exact timestamps (Mon 00:00 → Sun 23:59) in your org’s timezone. The backend stores in UTC but the UI should handle timezone display.

Rishi Malhotra: ok. any limits on range/size? don’t want it to fail and look dumb :)

Allison Grant: there are limits. If you go too wide you can hit timeout / row caps.
- max time range for export is currently 31 days
- there’s a max rows cap (you’ll see a warning in the modal if your filters are too broad)
If it fails, narrow by project/env, or export route list first (no model breakdown) then do a few targeted route detail exports.

Dev Patel: +1. We had a couple internal load tests where “all routes + model breakdown + 30d” was too big.

Rishi Malhotra: what’s the flow after I click export? does it download immediately?

Logan Wright: it creates an export job and then you’ll get a “Downloads” link in the toast (and also in the Exports panel). It’s not instant for big ranges.

Kevin Osei: FYI for Finance/security: export + download are audit-logged. You’ll see an audit event with who exported, which org/project, time range, and filters. (No prompt contents.)

Rishi Malhotra: good to know. Finance also asked if the export “matches the invoice” — I assume not 1:1?

Mei Lin: it’ll be close but not guaranteed 1:1. Common differences:
- **freshness/late arrival**: metering events can arrive late; invoice is finalized later
- **rounding** and aggregation windows
- **retention / missing route tags**: anything without route can show up as `unknown_route`
- **credits/discounts/taxes**: invoice includes billing adjustments; export is usage attribution
If they need reconciliation, use the “change vs prior period” view for trend + treat invoice as source of truth for billing totals.

Dev Patel: Support has a canned blurb for “console vs invoice mismatch” if you need it; happy to paste.

Rishi Malhotra: please paste. I’ll forward to Finance.

Dev Patel: here’s the short version:
“Usage Insights exports are intended for operational attribution (which routes/models drove spend) and may differ from invoice totals due to timing of metering data, rounding, and billing adjustments (credits/discounts). For billing reconciliation, use the invoice as the source of truth; for internal chargeback/trend analysis, use route-level exports with a consistent time window and project filters.”

Rishi Malhotra: perfect.

Paula Mendes: one more gotcha: if you want model fallback attribution, we attribute cost to the original route (good) but the model field will reflect the **actual** model used. So you may see multiple models per route even if the app “asked for” one.

Rishi Malhotra: that’s actually useful.

Allison Grant: if the job fails, check the toast error + try:
1) reduce range
2) switch to CSV without model breakdown
3) filter to region/env
and if it still fails, ping #eng-platform with the export job id.

Rishi Malhotra: just ran a test export for last 7d, CSV + model breakdown, filtered to Hosted / us-east. It completed in ~20s and downloaded. Looks good.

Kevin Osei: nice. also: download links expire after a short period (by design). If Finance needs it later, re-export with the same filters.

Rishi Malhotra: got it. thanks all — sending to Finance now.
